trickyParts: The one-lifecycle-row-at-a-time rule is in the outbox's shared SQL predicate (outboxLaneFree), not only in the lane goroutine as the plan's D3/D5 placed it. The real-binary proof found the gap: a due lifecycle row whose issue has a lifecycle sibling under a live lease held by another daemon was listed and claimed by this daemon's lane, so a rolling restart could run one issue's lifecycle rows side by side across the two daemons, and HeldRows (which lists exactly such rows) disagreed with what the lane did. With the rule in SQL, DueRows, ClaimRow and HeldRows agree by construction; HeldRows is the rule negated (its `not (outboxClaimable)` clause is implied and present only to bind the shared parameters, as its comment says).

The daemon API contract is 26, not the plan's 25: main took 25 for LEGION-636 (`source` on capability rows) while this branch was open and that release lacks heldOutboxRows, so the branch renumbered per docs/solutions/legion/daemon-api-contract-collision-renumber-when-the-release-declaring-the-number-lacks-your-shapes.md; main's 25 entry is kept verbatim in version.go and the CHANGELOG. The bump relaunches every live claim at deploy (the stale-plugin relaunch), as 23-25 did.

LaunchBound at the production defaults is 1h15m41s (3 boot timeouts + the launcher backstop of 2 boot timeouts + 30 min + 1 s + the 10 s termination grace + 71 x 30 s), above the plan's ~50 min estimate: a replacing try with six launcher roles makes 46 bounded calls in the rig, and relaunchCalls (17 per try + 9 per role x 6 roles) counts every retry and rare branch, since the one thing criterion 6 forbids is a bound shorter than a legitimate try. The bound is reached only by a try that hangs past every step's own deadline; the per-step bounds end a normal failure far earlier.

Two forward merges of main were needed (GitHub reported CONFLICTING twice): first over LEGION-636's contract 25 (version.go, version.json, pi-legion package.json and CHANGELOG), then over #1994's launch backoff (relaunch.go, sandbox.go, supervision_test.go); both resolved keeping both sides, every suite re-run green on the merged tree, each with its fingerprint comment on the pull request. In the merged relaunch, the bounded try context is what main's resend reads its deadline from, so a server-busy backoff ends at the launch bound like every other wait.

A renewal tick in flight when a row settled could find the row gone and log a false 'lease lost'; renewOnce and warnHeld check renewal.ended() after their reads so a settled row's tick reports nothing.

Round 2: the cross-daemon lane rule needed more than the SQL predicate. Two daemons claiming two different lifecycle rows of one issue update different rows, so neither waits on the other's row lock, and each update's outboxLaneFree subquery runs in its own READ COMMITTED snapshot where the other's uncommitted lease is invisible (write skew; the tester's red test). ClaimRow now takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock keyed by the issue for a lifecycle row before the update; a board row or a finished row selects no lock; the lock is released at the claim's commit, never held across an executor; intake.ApplyFact's advisory lock is a different key and no transaction takes both.

Round 2: the new CI race step's first run (38954475696) reported five races, all in three pre-existing tests reading a bytes.Buffer log sink while a daemon goroutine still wrote it (TestWorkflowBootLogsItsDependencyOrder, TestPollHoldReleaseWarnsWhenAHoldPersistsPastItsBound, TestAKubernetesDaemonServesItsWorkerStreamOnTCPAndRunsNoHostPaneMachinery); none in outbox_lanes.go or the store. Those sinks are the package's syncBuffer now and run 38956917435's race step is green.

The pod cannot run `go test -race` (no cgo), the Stage 1 script (its free-port.sh refuses the pod's 16000-65535 ephemeral range; no tmux or ss), the 31 NATS-bound daemon tests, the pgvector-bound ScratchDispatch tests or TestATerminalAttempt* (gVisor's /proc/self/status has no SigIgn): CI runs each of those on this head, and since round 2 the race detector over internal/daemon and internal/record as its own step.

Round 3: READY was refused at 8c1442d7 (READY_HEAD_CONFLICTS: 17 commits on main since bff10725, 18 files on both sides). The forward merge kept both sides of seven conflicts; the one judgement was the contract number: main's #1986 took 27 above this PR's reserved 26, so the constant, pi-legion's manifest and version.json land at 27 following main, this PR's 26 entry stays in version.go between 25 and 27 (and in the CHANGELOG after 27's), and no release ever declares 26 — the collision note's rule read from the other side. #1986's defaultBranch read in provisionWorkspace runs before provisionMu is taken (a GitHub read never holds the clone's lock), and the lane tests' outbox literal supplies defaultBranch: mainBranch as main's outbox tests do.
deviations: Plan D3/D5 placed the lifecycle one-at-a-time rule in the lane goroutine alone; it is also in the SQL predicate (outboxLaneFree), for the cross-daemon reason above. The plan's D11 four shapes of HeldRows are unchanged.
Plan §3 bumped the contract to 25; it is 26 (collision with LEGION-636).

Plan D8 estimated the bound at about 50 minutes; it is 1h15m41s at the defaults, generous by the plan's own rule. relaunchCalls is a package var (17 + 9 x len(claim.Roles)) rather than a const; fake.Runtime's field is TryBound (a Go struct cannot have a field and method both named LaunchBound).
HeldRows takes an issue filter ("" = every issue) so the lease tick's held-row read is one issue's, an efficiency finding of the simplify pass; the projection passes "".

The architect ruled (plan §10.1) that no operator Stage 3 run is asked for: criterion 7 is proven on the real binary in the pod, criteria 1-6 on the daemon's Postgres harness and CI, and the production check is the live proof of the loop.
